title: The Part Under the Water
subtitle: How to architect software natively with AI
notes: Spoken text uses Gemini TTS tags <short pause> and <long pause>; subtitles strip them. Numbers are spelled as spoken; visuals show digits.

beats.text: It's Tuesday morning. A message pops up: can we load this table from Statistics Netherlands, every day?
beats.visual: Night-blue room at dawn, a desk with a laptop. A chat bubble pops in with the question and a small generic table icon (no CBS logo).

beats.text: One sentence. <short pause> Ten years ago, that started a meeting. Today, you paste it into an AI agent, and code appears in minutes.
beats.visual: A calendar 'meeting' card pops up, then folds away. An agent window opens and lines of code stream in fast.

beats.text: Meet Tip. Tip is a small iceberg, and like every iceberg, most of Tip is under water.
beats.visual: Camera pans down to a calm sea. Tip (round iceberg with a face) bobs up and waves; the water clears to reveal a huge mass below the waterline.

beats.text: That turns out to be the whole story of building software with AI.
beats.visual: Tip winks. Title card: 'The Part Under the Water' with subtitle 'How to architect software natively with AI'.

beats.text: Zoom out. Nine out of ten technology professionals now use AI at work.
beats.visual: Zoom out from the desk to a crowd of ten people icons; nine light up. Counter ticks to 90%. Caption: DORA 2025.

beats.text: Almost three quarters of developers use coding assistants or agents every single day.
beats.visual: Calendar strip of days, each with a small agent icon. Counter ticks to 73%. Caption: Stack Overflow survey 2026.

beats.text: But trust has not kept up. <short pause> Only about one in six developers trusts AI with most everyday tasks. About half trust it when they can easily check the answer.
beats.visual: Two bars: a short one '16% · most everyday tasks' and a taller one '48% · when I can check' with a magnifying glass.

beats.text: And speed is harder to pin down than it feels. One careful study found experienced developers slower with early twenty twenty-five tools, and a little faster with later ones.
beats.visual: Two stopwatches side by side: 'early 2025 · slower' (hand runs past the goal) and 'late 2025 · a little faster'. Caption: METR.

beats.text: Google's DORA research puts it simply: AI doesn't fix a team. <short pause> It amplifies what's already there.
beats.visual: An amplifier dial turns up. A neat block structure grows taller and neater; a messy one grows into a bigger mess. Quote card.

beats.text: Here's why. The code an agent writes is the tip of the iceberg. It's what everyone sees.
beats.visual: Tip above the water; small code symbols </> sparkle on the tip. Little spectator eyes look at the tip.

beats.text: What decides whether that code is any good sits below the waterline.
beats.visual: Camera dives below the surface. The underwater mass glows faintly, still unlabelled.

beats.text: Principles that guide every choice. Interfaces that people and agents share. Context the agent can read. And checks that catch mistakes.
beats.visual: Four layers light up in spoken order, top to bottom: Principles, Shared interfaces, Written context, Checks.

beats.text: AI made the tip cheap. <short pause> So the real work moved under the water.
beats.visual: A price tag on the tip drops to almost nothing. A spotlight slides down onto the four layers.

beats.text: Take the data platform I build. It starts from five principles, and every change is checked against all five.
beats.visual: Zoom into the 'Principles' layer. Five tiles pop in: Clean UX, API first, AI native, Open source, Loosely coupled.

beats.text: API first means every button is an API call. So a script can do anything a person can.
beats.visual: A portal button connects by a line to a route chip 'POST /runs'. A script icon presses the same chip.

beats.text: AI native means agents are users too. Every API call is also a tool an agent can use, through the Model Context Protocol, with the person's own identity and rights.
beats.visual: The route chip duplicates into a tool chip labelled MCP. An agent character takes it, wearing the same ID badge as the person.

beats.text: In the pipelines extension, that's thirty tools. If a tool and its API call ever drift apart, a test fails.
beats.visual: Counter ticks to 30; a grid of 30 tool chips, each paired with a route chip. One pair drifts apart and a red test cross pops.

beats.text: The protocol itself is open. By the end of twenty twenty-five it had moved to the Linux Foundation, with more than ten thousand public servers.
beats.visual: A generic plug icon in the centre; dots for servers spread around it; counter ticks to 10,000+. Caption: Linux Foundation · Agentic AI Foundation.

scenes.title: A brilliant colleague with no memory

beats.text: The second thing to know about agents: an agent is like a brilliant new colleague who arrives every morning with no memory of yesterday.
beats.visual: A small agent character walks through a door each morning (sun rises three times); its thought bubble is empty each time.

beats.text: So what matters can't live in your head. <short pause> It has to live in files.
beats.visual: Thought bubbles leave a person's head and turn into document icons on a shelf.

beats.text: An agents file in every project tells the agent how to work there. More than sixty thousand open-source projects already have one.
beats.visual: AGENTS.md document icon. Counter ticks to 60,000+. Caption: agents.md.

beats.text: Skills are recipes for recurring jobs, like building a semantic model. And design records explain why a choice was made, before any code exists.
beats.visual: A SKILL.md recipe card, then a design-record document with a 'WHY' stamp; no code icon yet.

beats.text: DORA names this as one of the capabilities that make AI pay off: connect AI to your internal context.
beats.visual: A cable plugs the agent into the shelf of documents; its thought bubble fills. Quote card.

beats.text: Back to Tuesday's question. Before writing code, the agent reads the code that's already there.
beats.visual: The chat bubble from scene 1 returns. The agent scans a repository tree with a magnifying glass.

beats.text: It finds that pipeline runs have no internet, on purpose. So it proposes a separate extension for loading data, behind the same contract.
beats.visual: A run box with a padlock 'no internet'. A new box 'Loading' slides in and plugs into the same contract socket as the pipelines box.

beats.text: It checks every licence, finds a library with copyleft terms, and swaps it for an open one.
beats.visual: Library cards pass a scanner; one is flagged amber; it is swapped for a green card.

beats.text: It compares newer tools. Then I decide: keep one as a candidate, and test it in a spike.
beats.visual: Three tool cards. A human hand picks one and puts it in a tray labelled 'Candidate · spike'.

beats.text: Each step is checked against the five principles. And when code does come, the agent runs the full test suite, like the build server would, before it says done.
beats.visual: The five principle tiles tick green. A row of pipeline steps lights up one by one; 'done' appears only after the last step.

beats.text: The agent researches and proposes. <short pause> The people decide.
beats.visual: Split frame: the agent with a stack of documents on the left, a person with a decision stamp on the right.

beats.text: It's still Tuesday. The one-line question now has an answer: a design record, a principles check, and a plan for a spike.
beats.visual: The desk from scene 1. A reply bubble pops in with three attachments: Design record, Principles check, Spike plan.

beats.text: Not one line of production code yet. <short pause> But when it comes, the agent can write it fast, because everything under the water is in place.
beats.visual: Back to the sea: Tip's underwater layers are all lit. Code blocks stack quickly on the tip.

beats.text: AI makes the tip cheap. <short pause> So build the part under the water.
beats.visual: Tip smiles; the title returns; transition to the end card.

endCard.title: The Part Under the Water
